help_intro: Your stack will never match anyone's CV exactly, so I don't sell a particular technology; I sell a solved business problem. My core is production LLM systems. Around it I rely on a method rather than a claim: map the code first, pin down what it does today with tests, then change it, with every change checked by a reviewer that did not write it. That is how I added a security feature to a 20-year-old Rails application on a stack I had never used.

help.title: Build an AI product or feature
help.desc: From a business goal to a feature in production, with an evaluation baseline so you know it works before your users depend on it. Fixed scope, priced per deliverable.

help.title: Make an LLM system reliable
help.desc: Your RAG or agent works in the demo and fails in production. I find out why and fix it. You get a ranked failure report and the fixes.

help.title: Get ready for SOC 2 or ISO 27001
help.desc: I review your code and infrastructure for security, tighten access control and secrets handling, set up monitoring and incident response, and prepare the controls and documentation your audit will ask for.
help.fit: For teams facing a security review or certification

help.title: Take over legacy code
help.desc: Old, critical code that nobody on the team wrote and nobody dares to touch. I map it, pin down what it does today with tests, then change it safely.
help.fit: For teams with code older than the team

cases.title: When hiring stopped adding output
cases.problem: The business grew by launching new apps, and the 12-person team I led had hit a ceiling: every new hire added coordination rather than output.
cases.did: I built and ran an automated software factory: AI agents that design and code the apps, each output checked by an independent verifier, with a cost limit on every run.
cases.result: One engineer and one QA engineer outshipped the whole team.
cases.details: Multi-agent pipeline covering design, code, store assets and promo websites; model routing by task across Claude, Gemini and OpenAI; LLM-as-judge audits on a severity rubric. Architected its Google Cloud platform (Gemini and Claude on Vertex AI, Cloud Run, IAP, Secret Manager, Cloud Logging) and multimodal text-and-image search over the company's catalogue of 2,000+ apps. Replaced a paid low-code admin platform with an in-house dashboard. In my last week: 10 production apps in 3–4 days against the team's plateau of about 8 a week, at about $6 per app in model APIs.

cases.title: Changing old, critical code safely
cases.problem: Large codebases that nobody on the current team wrote, running in production.
cases.did: Four years of third-line support on enterprise systems, and recently a security feature in a 20-year-old Rails application on a stack I had never used.
cases.result: After the tests passed, red-team agents attacking a running instance found an authentication regression, a privilege escalation and a way around one of the fixes. Each was fixed and pinned by a regression test.
cases.details: 2006–2010 at EPAM: on the maintenance team of a large Thomson Reuters programme I diagnosed production failures with the client's engineers, migrated a live database while changing its schema, and coordinated deployments. 2026: personal access tokens for Redmine 6.1.2 (Ruby on Rails), built with code maps, implementing subagents and a five-axis verification gate: 39 issues, 75 recorded attacks, 4,674 lines of tests, with the full process record published next to the code.

cases.title: Four unfamiliar problems, four working systems
cases.problem: Video production was new territory for me: animation, audio processing, rendering and voice.
cases.did: I measured each problem before building anything, then directed AI coding agents to build the systems behind tests and review gates.
cases.result: Four working production systems, built in nine days to two months each, with episodes published on two YouTube channels.
cases.details: A desktop app that turns a sound recording into an audio-reactive animated video (audio analysis, GLSL shaders, a deterministic export through ffmpeg). A cartoon news show where every frame is rendered from code: Python vector art, code-generated skeletal animation and fact-checked scripts; a 6-minute episode renders in under 8 minutes. A narrated exercise series: parallel frame-by-frame rendering about 3.5× faster than serial, and narration aligned to the script without stretching the voice. A script-to-video pipeline with an animated 3D presenter rendered in Unity, its motion calibrated against recorded footage. Three of the four projects kept architecture decision records (ADRs), 70 to 200+ each.

cases.title: New distribution for a 200-app portfolio
cases.problem: I owned a portfolio of about 200 mobile apps end to end and worked with the business owners on budgets and ROI to keep it profitable.
cases.did: On my own initiative I tested two additional app stores, brought the numbers to the business and, once it approved, ran the full launch.
cases.result: Two new distribution channels, released from the same codebase as everything else.
cases.details: Huawei AppGallery and Samsung Galaxy Store, next to Google Play, Amazon and Xiaomi: five stores from one Android codebase with per-store builds. A shared app template reused 80–90% of the code.

process.title: Start from the business number
process.desc: What is it worth if it works, and what does it cost when it fails? That decides the architecture and the budget, including where an LLM is the wrong tool.

process.title: Build the evaluation first
process.desc: A test set and a scoring rubric come before the feature, so that "better" is a number rather than an opinion.

process.title: Verify independently
process.desc: Generation is cheap; verification is the bottleneck. Every output passes checks that the agent which produced it does not control.

process.title: Hand over something you own
process.desc: The code, the evaluation harness and the documentation stay with you, and so does the knowledge of how it works.

about: I'm a physicist by training. I started out writing C++ simulations for CERN's LHC experiments, then spent more than 20 years building software and leading engineering teams.

I founded a mobile games studio and grew it to a team of seven, negotiating partnerships with publishers and ad networks and running hiring, finances and KPIs. I was brought in as interim COO to stabilise a startup, analysing its profitability and guiding a pivot. For six years I was the lead engineer at a mobile-app company, working with the business owners on budgets and ROI and with the executive team on strategy. I have worked remotely since 2010.
In 2025 I rebuilt my own delivery around AI. The lesson I took from it: generation isn't the bottleneck, verification is.

cta.title: Have an AI product to build, an LLM system to fix or a security review to get ready for?
cta.text: Send me a few lines about the problem and the outcome you want. If AI is the wrong tool for it, I'll tell you.
